approach.comment: Self-described as a 'parser combinator inspired set of utility methods' built on the Iterator interface — a `Tokens` trait with combinator-style methods (many, sep_by, optional, surrounded_by, one_of), not a grammar generator.

implementation.comment: Zero runtime dependencies, so no C/C++ anywhere in the tree.

documentation.comment: No dedicated book; docs.rs crate-level docs plus an `examples/` folder are the documentation.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; 0.12.0 published 2023-11-18, no yanked or prerelease versions. All research reflects 0.12.0.

grammar-class.comment: Combinator-style methods over an iterator; no formal grammar class is imposed (per Assessment Guidelines).

grammar-definition.comment: Parsers are ordinary Rust functions taking `&mut impl Tokens`; the only macro is the declarative `one_of!` helper.

left-recursion.comment: No Pratt/precedence helper exists; a left-recursive function would recurse infinitely, so the grammar must be rewritten by hand.

ambiguity-handling.comment: 'Backtracking by default' — provided functions do not consume input on failure, and `one_of!` tries alternatives in order, rewinding between them.

backtracking.comment: `Tokens::location()` / `set_location()` allow saving and rewinding to any earlier position; there is no cut/commit operator.

lexer-integration.comment: Scannerless over `&str` (`StrTokens` yields `char`), and `SliceTokens` / `IterTokens` accept any `&[T]` or `Iterator + Clone` of tokens; the repo ships a `json_logos.rs` example pairing it with logos.

precedence-pratt-support.comment: No operator-precedence or Pratt facility in the `Tokens` trait or helper modules.

unicode-aware.comment: `StrTokens` iterates `char`s, computes the next char boundary before slicing, and its location is a byte index into the string.

input-types.comment: `StrTokens` for `&str`, `SliceTokens<T>` for any `&[T]` (covers `&[u8]` and token slices), `IterTokens` for any `Iterator + Clone`; the `Tokens` trait is public and user-implementable.

streaming-partial-input.comment: No 'need more input' signal in the core crate; the third-party `yap_streaming` extension (Easyoakland, 0.2.0, Nov 2023) adds stream parsing on top.

zero-copy.comment: `Tokens::slice(from, to)` returns a zero-copy `Tokens` over a range between two saved locations; `StrTokens::remaining()` hands back the unconsumed `&str`.

span-tracking.comment: `Tokens::offset()` / `location()` are always available; for `StrTokens` the location is a byte index, for slices/iterators an element offset. No line/column tracking.

output-model.comment: Parsing functions return whatever Rust type the user constructs (`Option<T>` / `Result<T, E>`); `parse()` converts consumed tokens via `FromStr`.

semantic-actions.comment: Values are built inside closures passed to `many`, `sep_by`, `optional`, `surrounded_by`, etc., and via ordinary Rust control flow around `Tokens` calls; there is no separate grammar/action layer.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: Whitespace is skipped explicitly with `skip_while(|c| c.is_whitespace())` or similar; no implicit skip rules.

stateful-parsing.comment: `Tokens::with_context()` / `with_context_mut()` wrap the token stream in `WithContext` / `WithContextMut`, carrying arbitrary user state through the parse.

error-recovery.comment: No recovery or synchronisation API; failed parses rewind and return `None` / `Err` to the caller.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: No error-accumulation mechanism; functions return a single `Option` / `Result`.

expected-token-reporting.comment: The crate defines no error type at all, so no expected-token sets are produced; users build their own errors.

custom-error-types.comment: Stated design goal: 'Allow user defined errors to be returned anywhere that it might make sense'; `_err` variants (`many_err`, `sep_by_err`, `optional_err`) propagate whatever `E` the user's closure returns.

error-span-fidelity.comment: yap ships no error type; the user attaches `Tokens::offset()` (a single byte/element offset) to their own errors. Ranges are possible by saving two locations, but nothing is provided out of the box, so rated 3 (single offset).

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: Zero dependencies and no documented bridge to ariadne/miette/codespan/annotate-snippets.

contextual-error-messages.comment: `with_context()` threads user *state*, not error labels; there is no `context`/`labelled`-style mechanism for annotating sub-parsers.

incremental-reparsing.comment: One-shot iterator-based parsing; no tree reuse.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Produces user-defined values, not a CST.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: crates.io reverse dependencies (2026-09-19) list scale-value, scale-info-legacy, doxygen-bindgen, simple-tokenizer, yap_streaming — no editor or LSP.

runtime-speed-tier.comment: No independent benchmark found. The crate itself says it 'aims to be fairly quick' and avoids allocations but that 'there may be quicker alternatives' if maximum speed is needed.

compile-time-impact.comment: No measurements found. Circumstantially light (about 2K lines, zero dependencies, no proc-macros), but per guidelines `null` rather than a guess.

allocation-strategy.comment: 'Avoids allocations (and allows you to do the same via the iterator-centric interface) almost everywhere'; combinators return lazy `Tokens`/`Iterator` impls rather than collections, and the crate builds without `alloc`.

no-std-support.comment: `#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]`; `default = []` so the crate is no_std by default and does not require `alloc`. The `std` feature is opt-in. lib.rs shows the no-std badge.

msrv.comment: No `rust-version` in Cargo.toml (crates.io reports null for every version) and no MSRV statement in the README; edition 2021.

unsafe-usage.comment: One `unsafe { self.str.get_unchecked(..) }` in `StrTokens::next()` after computing the char boundary; no `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, no unsafe in tokens.rs.

dependency-count.comment: No `[dependencies]`; only dev-dependency is logos 0.12 for the example.

wasm-compatible.comment: Inferred: pure Rust, zero dependencies, no_std by default, no I/O — nothing target-specific. Not explicitly tested for wasm in CI as far as found.

async-friendly.comment: Token types are plain structs over `&str` / `&[T]` / a `Clone` iterator (auto-`Send` when the underlying data is) and hold no interior state. Note there is no async input adaptor; consuming an async stream needs buffering (or the third-party `yap_streaming`).

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads on 2026-09-19; lib.rs shows ~251K/month, largely via scale-value / scale-info-legacy in the Parity/subxt ecosystem.

last-release.comment: 0.12.0. docs.rs shows a later build date for this version, but the crates.io publish timestamp is authoritative.

maintenance-status.comment: Last release 2023-11-18; last substantive commits Nov 2023; only a README typo fix (Feb 2025) since. Repo not archived, no seeking-maintainer notice. Checked 2026-09-19.

documentation-quality.comment: `#![deny(missing_docs)]` with examples on almost every function plus `examples/json.rs` and `json_logos.rs`; no tutorial, book, or migration guides.

tutorial-book.comment: API docs and an examples folder only.

notable-users.value: scale-value and scale-info-legacy (Parity Technologies, part of the subxt SCALE-codec tooling)
notable-users.comment: Both Cargo.toml files verified (`yap = "0.12.0"`, optional in scale-value). The yap author (jsdw / James Wilson) also maintains these Parity crates, so adoption is largely in-house.

bus-factor.comment: Essentially all commits by jsdw (James Wilson); lib.rs lists 2 other contributors with trivial changes.
